body_text:
Fundamental theorem of calculus, first part. If
$f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuous and $F(x)=\int_a^x f(t)\,dt$,
then $F$ is continuous on $[a,b]$, differentiable on $(a,b)$, and
$F'(x)=f(x)$ for every $x\in(a,b)$. Thus integration produces an
antiderivative of a continuous function.
